utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Both in and outside the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Again, are you able to help us as to how many people were already there before your arrival? Sorry, upon your arrival.

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it's again a matter of opinion, really, and I should say there were not less than 80 and not more than 120.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, were they people who had been formerly at either the barracks or the mosque; did you recognise any of them from there?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you first got there, is this right, that you were told first to wait at the first hangar?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we arrived there, those troops who had brought us told us to wait there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would this be right, as you told the OTP, that there were some 30 to 40 standing outside the hangar, and those people had already received their passes?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: By "pass", Mr. G, I mean a pass enabling them to be released from the camp.

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what pass that was. But whatever the case, they were standing there, waiting to be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour will forgive me. I forgot to deal with one matter concerning something which happened at the mosque, and I'll return to that now, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Mr. G, forgive me if we just go back a little bit. I forgot to put one matter to you. The man called Papa, Ahmed Hodzic or Hadzic, is this right, that firstly he was a local community leader and a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: He used to say that he was a member of the SDA and president of a neighbourhood community, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you personally witness him being beaten?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: While they were beating them there in the hallway of the mosque, at that time, yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was it being made clear that the reason he was being beaten was because of his connections with the SDA and his place in the community?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I thought that that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll return now back to the front of the hangar, if I may, and I'm grateful for enabling me to go back. Were you initially kept at the front of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You were able to see people being taken to the office?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Is this right, that some of those were returning to your group with passes?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not my group; the group across, across from our group.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So that the initial group that you saw standing outside the hangar was being increased by people coming out of the hangar, going to the offices, being interrogated; do you know?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Coming out of the offices and joining that first group?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: While I was there, two or three joined that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: That group that already had passes, was it subsequently released that day or that night?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Towards the evening, towards late afternoon, they were released, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How long did you remain outside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean in terms of time? I am afraid I did not have any sense of time. I said we were taken in by Goran Jelisic. It was a short time before the nightfall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were you able to discover anything about the interrogations that were taking place?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to ask you now about the killings which you say that you observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If Your Honours would just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What you told us today and what you told the Office of the Prosecutor was that the first person you saw with Goran was taken around the corner of a building and out of your sight. May we take it from that that you did not, in fact, see anybody being killed?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And the extent of the information that you can give Their Honours is that the person you saw, the person you described as Goran, did not reappear?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: What do you mean? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The most that you can tell us is that one of the persons who went around the corner, the detainee, did not reappear?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Goran reappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes, but not the detainee? I'm interested in --

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. He did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And you're quite sure that you saw absolutely nothing of the killing, or a killing, at that stage?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So that you may deal with it, Mr. G, please, can you explain why, in your statement to the Bosnia-Herzegovina authorities, you claimed to have seen a killing at that stage then, in relation to the first person that you saw?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: It seems I have to say that, again, that was not the way I put it to the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was how it was put to me. And I did not want to come for the second or for the third time, because the second or the third person, that was the same kind of thing, said here and there. Do you know when it was that I gave my statement to the Bosnia-Herzegovina authorities? They were writing it with a pencil, and on the basis of all the statements of all the people they interrogated at the time, they then made probably one statement. And I would have had to go back there and to be exposed again to all that I had been already exposed to. As to the substance, there is no difference, there is no discrepancy. I did not see the first one, but I saw the second one being killed. And I just really didn't want to go into it; I didn't want to discuss it with them. And besides, they also told me that it was only for their internal use. I didn't feel like going back there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Mr. G, I want to make sure exactly the circumstances in which you gave this account. You said to their Honours just now -- and I'm reading from your evidence -- "That was not the way I put it to the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was how it was put to me." Are you saying that you were told what to put in that statement?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I said the same thing as I said afterwards, that is the sequence and all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So where your statement to the Bosnia-Herzegovina authorities differs from that which you made to the Office of the Prosecutor, that may be explained by you being persuaded to put in things which were not true?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: As regards the substance, I'm telling you, the first or the third, there is no difference in substance. I'm saying that I said what I had told them, and I said the same here, except that when they were putting it together, when they were writing it out, typing it out, then the third person appeared to be the first. That is, the third person that I talked about to them, they put it in the first place, and the other way. But basically what I said was that I saw with my own eyes one murder, and I don't see what else I have to say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think we'll move on. As far as any conversation about handing over of valuables and so on, I suggest to you that that is not correct, that did not happen.

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I say that it did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can you help us with this. The group that were in fact released, can you say at what time it was they were released? Was it close to curfew time?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And so that we may know what time that was, at what time was the curfew on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. Because one of those troops said, "Well, if you are releasing them, let us release them before the curfew." And I know when they were released, they all started running towards the exit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You were able to see them leaving. Was Goran still there when they left and able to see them leaving?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I suppose he could. I was in the hangar, right across the door. I saw them leave. Of course, I could not follow them all the time, but insofar as the door was open, I could see them leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As far as the account which you give of Goran coming in and getting you all to sing songs and conducting that exercise, again, I suggest that that did not happen.

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say that it did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Although it is right to say that you told the BiH authorities about being forced to sing songs, you said nothing to them about Goran directing and conducting the exercise, and in your statement to the Prosecutor, you made no mention at all of that incident; can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not say that it was somebody else either. It simply depends, and one doesn't really remember every little thing at any given moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: During the course of the night, when you'd been put into the hangar, are you saying that people were taken out as foursomes throughout the night at regular intervals?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Once every 15 minutes, once every 30 minutes? What are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it's again a matter of opinion. It wasn't all that quickly; not every 15 minutes. Some intervals were shorter and longer, but I cannot be more accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Again, what you told the BiH authorities was that three prisoners were taken out, and you made no mention of anything more than that. And --

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Three detainees. At the time when the light fell on me, they also lit up those three prisoners. But I do not know -- as for that statement, I don't think I could have omitted to mention that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Again, in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, you mention a total of seven people being taken out.

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said after that first time, when the light was thrown on me, that I know that people were being taken out, but I couldn't know how many. To begin with, it was a long time ago. Secondly, I was really trying to use that time to come to terms somehow with my fate, trying to find some encouragement within me. I was focusing on my own fate. And when somebody said -- and when Goran came back, I was trying to remember those things then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I misled the Court, in fact. The figure -- it's because I can't read my own writing. It should have been ten, not seven, and I apologise to Your Honour and the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It was ten, in all, that you mentioned, but in groups of three, three, and four, Mr. G.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we might take a break now.

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know where I could have made that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How long is the break for, so that we can go and see my client? All right. I'm sorry. I missed what Your Honour said. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can now resume the hearing. Please have the accused brought in, and be seated. Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Mr. G, can I just clarify something with you, please. And just to retrace my steps slightly, the issuing of passes on the night of May the 8th, that's the day on which you were transferred to Luka. Is it your evidence that the issuing of passes was taking place in the administration offices or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: From where the prisoners were taken to and then taken from.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was there a table inside the hangar where passes were being issued, passes for release?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: As I said, I don't know. With respect to the issuance of these passes, when I arrived there, people were standing in front of me inside the hangar, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were you able to see by whom the passes were being issued? Was it by an ordinary soldier, or a civilian, or somebody that you could identify, or -- help us with that.

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to ask you just one detail, please, about the man Stipo Glavocevic. You knew him before the war?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: He was working as a police officer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: He was of Croatian origin?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to clarify one thing that was said or that you may have said in relation to the person Jasce or Jasce. You told us about Goran coming in and asking a question. Can you just repeat the question again, because it's possible that your full answer may not have come out on the transcript. Can you tell us what exactly was said?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He said, "Let the person get up who cursed the Serbian waitress. I know who it is."

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: That's all you say that was said?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Something like that, so that this person should get up himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want next to ask you about the man who enabled you to be released. I don't want you to say his name in public, but would you be prepared, please, to write it down for the use of the Court?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know why the name is significant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, with respect, there may be information that we have concerning him that would enable us to, but I don't want to mention the name in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would respectfully invite my learned friend to show relevance before he compels the revelation of a name, the sensitivity of which is perhaps fairly obvious, for the person named assisted this man to safety and it may be there are concerns about this man's safety in the mind of the witness. Absent relevance, there's no need for us to reveal that name at all. Once it is revealed to the Defence lawyers, it's inevitably available to everyone within the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It is already within our possession, for obvious reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Move to another question, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I was going to say, Your Honour, that I didn't press the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In any event, that person arranged for you to get a pass. Is this also right, that -- and I don't want to know what the relationship was, but a relation of yours was also enabled to get a pass?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I got the pass, I stayed behind in order to attempt to perhaps work with this person in order for my relative to be issued another pass, but eventually he was not issued the pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How many people were released at the same time as you were?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the line in front of this room, we were -- Your Honours, this is all a matter of judgement. We were about 10 to 15. Sometimes when I state things like this, this is something that I say to the best of my recollection. They ask me to say exactly, but I say what I know best. So maybe later on, somebody again will ask me to say the exact number, and I may not even remember what I had said on a previous occasion when I was asked to give my best estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Mr. G, the answer that you've given is, "We were about 10 to 15." It would have been simpler, with respect to you, to have said, "We were about 10 to 15," if that's your answer. Thank you. I want to ask you now, please, about the beating of Naza Bukvic. Is this right, that your evidence is that Goran said, in relation to her, that her brother was the main sniper in the town?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So that the purpose and motive behind the beating was because her brother was a sniper?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps he made it a motive.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to ask you next, please, about you having seen Goran Jelisic again after your release from Luka.

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: No. Let me ask the question slightly more clearly. You left Luka, having been released on a pass. Subsequently, your evidence is that you saw Goran Jelisic on two further occasions, once at Batkovic camp and once when you were in a bus and persons pointed him out to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would you accept this, Mr. G, that in relation to your statement to the Bosnia-Herzegovina authorities, you did not mention at all seeing Goran Jelisic again, and in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, you only claimed to have seen him on one occasion at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: These statements, and let me repeat it, were given in different circumstances. When I was giving a statement for the Bosnia and Herzegovina authorities, I was answering questions, and whatever I was asked, these were the answers that I had given them. It is entirely possible that I had completely forgotten about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As far as learning what his name was, that is as a result of you being told by others what they believed to be his name; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to turn now, please, to the list of names. You will recall that with Mr. Nice, you went through a number of names, and I just want to ask a little bit more detail about that. The man Midhat Cembic, is this right: Was he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me remind you that you have about six or seven minutes left. Try to organise yourself accordingly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm hoping to be done, but I need to just go through these.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Midhat Cembic, Mr. G, is this right, that he was a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You heard that he had been labelled a sniper and that was the motive behind his killing. Did you hear any other details of that?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Regarding Midhat Cembic, when I was at the barracks, I know that a soldier walked in and asked us did anybody know Midhat Cembic. I did not respond at that time. Then he said, "Who would have thought that he was a sniper?" This is how I knew that he had been sort of pointed out as a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: This was as a result of something that somebody else said to you. Can you say when it was? Was any other information about when he had been killed given to you?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. (redacted) (redacted). Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like to turn, please, to the name Kasim Kartal. Is he one of two brothers who I think were at one stage involved heavily in football; is that right?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was either Kasim or his brother, to your knowledge, a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Galib Muranjkovic, you knew something about his being killed, is that right, Galib Muranjkovic?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I said that I did not meet him either during or after the war, but when I was at Batkovic, his son had been brought there and he said -- he related that his father was taken off a vehicle on the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of his father, the first name of his father?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Galib Muranjkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And the name of the son?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Son's name? Right now, I cannot recall it, but I know him and I would remember it at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Irfan Topalcevic, is this right, that you heard that he was killed at home? Did he live in the Kolobara district?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was he an SDA member, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Do you know when it was that you heard he had been killed? Was it right at the beginning of the conflict or at some later stage?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Later. Can you say how much later?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I learned about that later. When I came out from Luka, it was then that I heard that Irfan had been killed, and I heard it from his acquaintances who were in the same building where I was put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Mehmed Jakubovic, did he have a father called Muharem?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know anything about Mehmed Jakubovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So you don't know what his fate was?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Then -- and I'm coming fairly rapidly towards the end -- Sakib Becirevic; you heard that he was --

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Kibe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Kibe? I'm sorry? What did you say, Mr. G?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Kibe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You heard that he was killed behind the gymnasium; is that right?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And that was by somebody called Cesic?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Do you know if he was a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And can you say when the killing took place? Do you know any of that?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Dr. Edhemovic, again, do you know any of the -- the date when he was killed? Would that be 1993? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The Terzic brothers: We've got details of three of them, but were there in fact four brothers? Can you help us about that?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: They could have been Terzics.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Somebody called Mido Terzic?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. That wasn't him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like, then, to ask you this: You've identified someone as Kosta, the Chetnik, as having been, according to your information, the killer of at least one if not all of the brothers. Is Kosta the Chetnik, is that Kosta Kostic?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As far as -- is it your information that they were killed in the Kolobara district?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to what I heard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And Vasif Suljemanovic, you saw him late in 1992, sometime around October?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 4th or the 5th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Have you been given information that subsequently he was killed?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And finally, Osman Vatic: He was detained at Batkovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is, if that is the Osman Vatic without a leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the Osman Vatic without a leg, your information or your knowledge is that he was released; is that right?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Do you know the date upon which he was released, whether exactly or approximately?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't. I don't. He spent quite some time in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Do you think it was 1992, or 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And your information, again, was that he was killed at his home subsequent to his release?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I heard from other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: At the very end of 1992, or earlier than that?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Now, again, it's a matter of thinking, of estimating. I came out on the 4th of October, and he was released before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. G. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Greaves. Thank you for having respected the amount of time that was given to you. Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I have one topic to deal with in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witness G, you have been asked questions about your evidence to the effect that the man, Goran Jelisic, at the barracks, spoke to you and others about what was going to happen to you, generally, and it was suggested that you had said in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor that this happened on the 6th of May, and you denied that you'd said that in the statement, specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness have the B/C/S version of the English statement which was taken, I think, in English. I've sidelined each version with the passage that I'd like him to look at. It's not an exhibit yet, and unless the Chamber wants these statements to be exhibited, they needn't be. If the English version could go on the ELMO, and if the witness could follow in the B/C/S version as I read from the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Witness G, in your statement there is this passage: "During the afternoon of May the 6th, all the detainees in the mosque were transferred by bus to the army barracks. At the barracks, they put us in a big room near the kitchen. I saw Goran Jelisic and Kosta at the barracks. "Soldiers took all of us from the room to the front of the building. I was about 20 or 30 metres from him. Goran had a characteristic voice, was good-looking, had a bandage on his wrist, and he wore the light blue civilian police uniform. He was slightly taller than average height and had black hair. Goran said to us, 'All of you are going to come to me later.' He also said, '70 per cent of you should be killed, 30 per cent should be beaten up, and 4 per cent of the 30 per cent were probably good.' He cursed us and called us balijas. At that time I did not know Goran's identity; however, I later saw him at Luka. Goran left, and we went back into the room. This occurred around noon. I spent two days at the army barracks before I was transferred to Luka camp." And then it goes on to deal with Luka camp. Two things: Did Goran Jelisic say to you the things that you've set out in this statement? "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Of the two days that you were at the barracks, can you say on which day this happened?

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first day -- it certainly didn't happen on the first day, because we were brought there in the afternoon, and this happened sometime in the morning, that is, before noon. It was daylight. So it could have been either the 7th or the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: G (Resumed)
utterances.text: And here, when I was telling you it was the 6th of May, no, I was simply speaking about the events that happened, and I told you that we were brought there on the 6th, and then I was recalling all sorts of other things, but I did not say that it all happened on the 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I have no other re-examination of this witness. Nothing else from me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me turn to my colleagues. No questions? No questions? One point, but let me ask the Prosecutor, not

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, it seems that there is an inconsistency between the statement made to the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the statements that were taken by your office. If you don't want to answer, don't. Here's my question: When you interviewed Witness G, did you call his attention to those inconsistencies, or did you use the same reasons that had been used? Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think counsel can answer, because he wasn't -- according to the information -- present at the time when that interview took place, and I would be loath to get counsel to give evidence in the case, which wouldn't be a proper thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm grateful for the protection of my learned friend, but as to the statement, it's quite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Greaves, you have a very subtle way of reminding me of things, but I think that the Judges can ask certain questions, and I would like to know something about that point. And before you spoke, Mr. Greaves, you noted that I was very careful to say to the Prosecutor that if he didn't wish to answer, he didn't have to. Therefore, I didn't really need your advice. It was simply a question asked for clarification for the Tribunal. I could have asked the witness the question, but I thought it was much easier to ask the Prosecutor. But I keep my question that I asked Mr. Nice, and that he doesn't have to answer if he doesn't want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm quite happy to answer. In all matters, I feel that maximum --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought so. I thought so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As to the interview, of course, that is the statement that we've just been looking at. That was a statement taken well before I ever knew that I was ever likely to be at the Tribunal. It was taken by others. If Your Honour had in mind what's called, in accordance with the practices of this institution, the proofing session, I regret that I can't help you there completely, because I have fortune, good or bad, of having quite a lot of things to do, and the first -- the stage of proofing of the witness, I'm happy -- I'm fortunate enough to have someone else do that for me in the first stage, and I only spoke to the witness personally, myself, at the latter stage. I can find out for you, from the person who did the proofing of the first stage, whether the inconsistencies were drawn to the witness's attention, but I can certainly tell you that at the time I spoke to him myself -- which was shortly before he gave evidence; I think the day before -- I didn't draw those inconsistencies to his attention myself, because by that stage, matters were substantially already prepared and summarised. But I can certainly find out. I think, if it helps you, our approach would -- well, yes, our approach would probably be to deal with obvious inconsistencies where they seem significant, because that would be a sensible approach with the witness, and to get them resolved. But of course we may not spot every inconsistency, or we may not regard them always as significant. And, of course, the overriding concern is to know from a witness what his present recollection and account is, and unless there is any reason to trouble him or her with earlier inconsistencies for clarification, that may not always be gone into. But I can find out more about this witness. I can deal with the matter generally, if that would help you. And as to this witness, as with any witness -- we haven't exhibited the two statements, but -- and he's given an account of why the Bosnian statement is as it is. But I'm in the Court's hands. If the Court wants them to be exhibited, of course, they can be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I, myself, don't intend to go any further, even though I might say to Mr. Greaves that I'm allowed to by the Rules. But I have no further comments to make. I think the best thing to do, and I think everybody is agreed, starting with the interpreters, who must be tired after this long afternoon, I think that we should now adjourn today's session and resume tomorrow morning at 10.00. Would you like to add something, Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I would, please, if you wouldn't mind. We would invite you, at the very least, to have as an exhibit the statement made by this man to the Bosnia-Herzegovina authorities about which he has explained so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In which case, probably better for both to be exhibited, I would have thought, both the Bosnian one and the one to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mindful of the needs to maintain the rights of the accused, all of the statements should be tendered as evidence, and we'll ask the Registry to give them numbers. We will now adjourn and resume tomorrow at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May I detain the Court -- I think it will be convenient -- is it possible to go into what's called, I think, private session for 30 seconds? It's an administrative matter that I've been asked to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.
